- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% below the 14-day moving average to prevent false optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 3–5% in the next 3–5 days to allow mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3) and forecast is trending, align with 7-day moving average rather than 30-day trend.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.1) over 3+ days, suppress forecast upward bias — model tends to overestimate recovery.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid lagged overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is rising and forecast is flat, add 1–2% upward bias to reflect sentiment momentum.  
- Avoid forecasting above 10% above recent 14-day high unless sentiment is >0.7 and confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
